correctness.rationale: For two identical repulsive delta interactions, simplicity and positivity of the one-dimensional ground state force reflection symmetry through the two sites, hence equal positive endpoint amplitudes on both complementary arcs. Solving \(-u''=k^2u\) on an arc of length \(L\) with equal endpoint value gives the cosine profile and positivity forces \(0<kL<\pi\). The two delta jumps combine to \(lpha=k[\tan(ka/2)+\tan(kb/2)]\), which is strictly increasing in \(k\) on the positive branch. Strict convexity of \(\tan\) and \(a+b=2\pi\) then gives the unique antipodal maximizer for every \(lpha>0\). This is an analytic proof, not an inference from the finite transfer-matrix tests.
risks: The argument relies on the special two-site reflection symmetry and equal interaction strengths.
